title: Kanpur Plastipack Ltd - 507779 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Kanpur Plastipack Q1 FY27 standalone total income Rs 207.49 cr (first time above Rs 200 cr) and PAT up 112% YoY to Rs 12.14 cr, with EBITDA margin at 10.69%.
summary.overview: Standalone total income crossed Rs 200 crore for the first time, up Rs 13.86 crore YoY, while EBITDA rose 58.98% to Rs 22.19 crore and margin widened to 10.69% from 7.66%. Average selling price rose 31% QoQ against an 18% rise in raw material prices, though management said employee cost increases of about Rs 3-3.5 crore per quarter absorbed part of the gain. FIBC volume fell to about 3,000 tonnes from 3,500 tonnes a year earlier, due to polymer and labour disruptions. The premium polypropylene Taslan yarn JV with Essegomma (Italy) started commercial production and sales, with volume ramp guided from Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: from Rs 1.25 crore in Q1 FY26
from about Rs 112 crore long-term debt at 31 March 2026 (figures as stated; basis unclear)

segments.name: FIBC
segments.commentary: Cornerstone business at 52% of Q1 sales; volume 3,000 tonnes in Q1 vs 3,800 in Q3 FY26 and 3,500 in Q4 FY26. Management targets 5,000 tonnes per quarter by Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Premium PP Taslan yarn (ESSEKAN, Essegomma JV)
segments.commentary: Commercial production and sales began in Q1; about Rs 10 crore revenue expected in FY27 at 20-25% EBITDA margin, with a Rs 30 crore peak on current capacity.

segments.name: Non-woven technical textiles
segments.commentary: Facility on track for commissioning by Q3 FY27; revenue expected from Q3 FY27, mid-double-digit EBITDA guided on B2C non-woven.

segments.name: Valex Ventures (UK)
segments.commentary: Revenue described as timid with no significant tangible benefit yet; some customer supplies were shifted to after the first fortnight of July to align with the UK FTA.

guidance_outlook: ESSEKAN premium PP yarn revenue about Rs 10 crore in FY27 at 20-25% EBITDA; ambition of Rs 25 crore, Rs 50 crore, Rs 100 crore over the following years, with Rs 100 crore targeted in about four years.
Long-term revenue path: about Rs 900-950 crore in FY27-28 and Rs 1,000-1,050 crore in FY29 on installed capacity and current trading and polymer prices.
FIBC capacity to add 6,000 tonnes per annum over five years (about 1,200 tonnes a year); target 5,000 tonnes per quarter by Q1 FY28.
Non-woven: commercial production expected in FY27, commissioning by Q3 FY27; target IRR 15-20% and ROCE above 20%; working capital of 30-40 days on non-woven turnover.
Management expects to sustain the current EBITDA margin level but declined to give a precise full-year margin guide.
Employee cost increase expected to be mitigated over 12-18 months through cost, automation and productivity initiatives.

Debt: long-term debt Rs 34 crore now, about Rs 67-68 crore at year-end after a new Rs 40 crore term loan less Rs 5-7 crore repayments (CFO's year-end figure reads as Rs 74 crore before repayment, stated as near Rs 74 crore and then Rs 67-68 crore). Working capital about Rs 90 crore, rising Rs 5-10 crore by year-end.
capex_capacity: FIBC capacity expansion of 6,000 tonnes per annum over five years is on track; new building ground floor complete and production started, first and second floors due by mid-September 2026.
Non-woven fabric facility: construction and installation progressing; commissioning targeted by Q3 FY27.
ESSEKAN: management said capacity can deliver about Rs 30 crore revenue; further capacity to be added once 50-60% utilisation is reached, as capex needs are low.
FIBC quarterly volumes: Q3 FY26 3,800 tonnes, Q4 FY26 3,500 tonnes, Q1 FY27 3,000 tonnes; seasonal working-day effects cited.
Renewable power now about 60% of energy; annual savings about Rs 3-5 crore; battery storage a couple of years away.
demand_pricing: Average selling price up 31% QoQ vs raw material up 18% QoQ; management said realisations track raw material costs and are passed through with a lag of two weeks to one quarter.
Export mix: Europe about 60%, South America about 20%, North America about 16%, Australia and Asia about 4.5%, Africa about 0.5%; minimal West Asia exposure.
Demand visibility about four weeks as customers avoid buying at high prices; some customers building inventory on geopolitical risk while most are reducing it.
Polymer volatility eased from about plus/minus 25% in March to plus/minus 10% now.
Ocean freight rose from about $2,000 to $5,000 per container over the last two months; management flagged risk of lower demand and partial cost sharing with customers that could hit margins.
Employee cost rose about Rs 3-3.5 crore QoQ from annual salary revision and state minimum-wage hike; other cost pressures from packing, oil, freight and one-time disruption costs.

qa_highlights.question: Shubhi Gupta (Trinetra Asset Managers): How is raw material volatility from the West Asia conflict progressing, and can raw material moves be passed to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Polymer volatility has eased from about plus/minus 25% in March to plus/minus 10% now. Raw material changes are generally passed through with a lag of two weeks to one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Shubhi Gupta: What is the marginal differential and expected EBITDA from the B2C-linked premium segments, and what total EBITDA margin should be expected for the company?
qa_highlights.answer: ESSEKAN is expected to add about Rs 10 crore revenue in FY27 at 20-25% EBITDA; non-woven B2C is guided to mid-double-digit EBITDA. Management would not give an exact company-wide margin guide but expects to sustain current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor (Kapoor & Co): What is ESSEKAN's peak revenue on current capacity and when would more capacity be added?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity can reach about Rs 30 crore revenue. More capacity will be added once utilisation hits 50-60%, as the capex is not high.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: Why did margins not expand more despite the 31% ASP rise versus 18% raw material rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing EBITDA margin was 12.6%. Employee cost rose about Rs 3-3.5 crore QoQ, FIBC manufactured volume fell due to supply chain and labour disruptions, and there were packing, oil, freight and one-time disruption costs. Energy costs were not a significant increase.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What are the factors ahead for the rest of the year, and what are the FIBC capacity and mix plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Two risks: ocean freight rising from about $2,000 to $5,000 per container could dent demand, and partial sharing of costs with customers could hit margins. Target is 5,000 tonnes per quarter by Q1 FY28; management declined to give a product mix percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What was the FIBC utilisation and is 3,000 tonnes the base for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes were 3,800 tonnes in Q3 FY26, 3,500 in Q4 FY26 and 3,000 in Q1 FY27, with working-day seasonality. Management called 3,000 a damaged number that will build from here.

qa_highlights.question: Chaitrika (individual investor): What is the long-term revenue aspiration and what are the milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Current projects and installed capacity can take revenue to about Rs 900-950 crore in FY27-28 and Rs 1,000-1,050 crore in FY29, assuming current trading and polymer prices. Management will decide on deploying balance-sheet cash for further capacity next year.

qa_highlights.question: Yash Parker (individual investor): What tangible benefits have the UK (Valex) and Italian JV delivered, and when will financials show?
qa_highlights.answer: ESSEKAN sampling is under way with significant commercialisation expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27, with guidance on it by Q4. Valex has delivered no significant tangible benefit so far beyond brand awareness; its turnover is manufacturing-transferred, so profit sits within Kanpur Plastipack.

qa_highlights.question: Yash Parker: What annual savings come from renewable power, and what is the FIBC capacity ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewable power is about 60% of energy and already at the planned level, saving about Rs 3-5 crore a year. Battery storage is a couple of years away. FIBC adds about 1,200 tonnes a year, so 4-5 years to reach the full 6,000 tonnes.

qa_highlights.question: Yash Parker: What IRR and ROCE hurdles apply, and what working capital is needed as the business ramps?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-woven targets 15-20% IRR and ROCE above 20%; ESSEKAN returns are far higher given low capex. Working capital stays at similar levels for FIBC and raffia, while non-woven adds 30-40 days of working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Deeya Jain (Sapphire Capital): What are the realisation trends, and the ESSEKAN revenue targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisations track raw material and freight costs and should hold while raw material costs are steady. ESSEKAN is about Rs 10 crore in FY27, with an ultimate aim of Rs 100 crore in four years.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What is the impairment, contract value and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: The Rs 25 lakh provision relates to a Rs 15 crore government (FCI) coating tender supply, taken as a prudent provision. Long-term debt is Rs 34 crore now and about Rs 67-68 crore at year-end after a Rs 40 crore term loan and Rs 5-7 crore repayments. Working capital is about Rs 90 crore, rising Rs 5-10 crore by year-end.

risks_watch: Ocean freight up from about $2,000 to $5,000 per container could slow demand and force partial cost sharing with customers, pressuring margins.
Employee cost step-up of about Rs 3-3.5 crore per quarter; management expects to mitigate it only over 12-18 months through automation and productivity.
FIBC volume fell to 3,000 tonnes in Q1 FY27 from 3,800 in Q3 FY26; the 5,000 tonnes per quarter target by Q1 FY28 needs a sharp recovery.
ESSEKAN commercialisation depends on sampling and brand-owner approvals; significant sales are expected only in Q3-Q4 FY27, with guidance deferred to Q4.
Non-woven facility commissioning by Q3 FY27 and revenue from Q3 FY27 are still pending; the Valex UK business has shown no significant benefit yet.
Net debt figure (Rs 132 crore) and debt bridge were not clearly reconciled on the call; debt rises to about Rs 67-68 crore long-term by year-end with a new Rs 40 crore term loan.

summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's headline numbers and the ESSEKAN and non-woven pipeline, but cautious on near-term demand, freight and cost pressures. Management was evasive on a precise full-year EBITDA margin and product mix, and declined to quantify several targets beyond directional statements.
